subject: Urgent: Checkoutly surge — backpressure decision & customer comms
messages:
From: Alicia Park <apark@checkoutly.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@checkoutly.com
Date: 2028-10-19T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: High tail latency + throughput drop right now

Monica —

We just saw a sharp degradation: p99 generation latency jumped from ~260ms to ~1.8s and our throughput dropped ~45% across the last 12 minutes. This started roughly 08:25 PT. We have users timing out and the incident is visible in our dashboard.

Key details:
- Service: /v1/generate (standard chat model pinned to rdw-instruct-v2)
- Errors: negligible 5xx but lots of long tail timeouts on our side
- QPS: fell from 420 -> ~230

Can Redwood enable any immediate protective controls (rate backpressure, model variant fallback, temporary cache TTL adjustments) while we triage? We need a short customer-facing note we can post to our internal ops channel and customers (support).

Please loop in SRE/Eng and advise next steps.

—Alicia
Alicia Park
Head of Platform Ops, Checkoutly
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Park <apark@checkoutly.com>, ops@checkoutly.com
Date: 2028-10-19T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: RE: High tail latency + throughput drop right now

Thanks for the signal, Alicia — we’re on it. Looping in SRE and runtime. Initial read: looks like a burst of expensive long-context requests caused KV cache churn plus some kernel scheduling pressure on the worker pool.

Immediate mitigations I propose (can we action in the next 15–30m?):
- Apply a soft request-rate cap for Checkoutly route (token-based shed) to stabilize latency while preserving priority traffic.
- Temporarily increase KV cache TTL for recent prefixes (reduce cache eviction churn).
- If needed, shift Checkoutly to a lower-cost model variant with same semantics (rdw-instruct-v2-compact) for 30–60m as a staged fallback.

Ben / Karthik / Evelyn — can you confirm which of the above are fast toggles and whether we should also enable prefix prefetch to reduce recompute at tail?

Customer comms: Alicia, I’ll draft a short note below for your ops channel once we confirm the mitigations.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Alicia Park <apark@checkoutly.com>
Date: 2028-10-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: High tail latency + throughput drop right now

On Fri, Oct 19, 2028 at 08:55 AM Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Ben / Karthik / Evelyn — can you confirm which of the above are fast toggles and whether we should also enable prefix prefetch to reduce recompute at tail?

Quick status: I can flip two fast controls now without deploys:
1) Route-level soft token shed (limits accepted requests under surge) — immediate (config toggle).
2) Increase KV cache TTL for Checkoutly namespace from 60s -> 300s — immediate (control plane change).

We should be cautious with full prefetch — that requires a small release for safety and could temporarily raise per-request CPU if mis-sized. I recommend NOT prefetching until we see whether TTL + backpressure bring p99 down.

Fallback model: rdw-instruct-v2-compact is quantized and reduces per-token compute ~35%. Can stage canary traffic (10% -> 50%) over next 20–30m if TTL+shed not sufficient. That can also be done via routing config (no code changes).

I’ll implement token shed + TTL change now and report back in 8–10 minutes. Attaching a concise runbook for SRE steps.

[Attachment: runbook_backpressure_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

—Ben
Ben Carter
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime Performance
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Alicia Park <apark@checkoutly.com>, ops@checkoutly.com
Date: 2028-10-19T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: High tail latency + throughput drop right now

Monica / Ben — implemented the soft token shed and bumped Checkoutly KV TTL to 300s at 09:19 PT. Observed early signals:
- p99 down from 1.8s -> ~620ms within ~4 minutes.
- QPS recovering from 230 -> 320 (still below baseline).

Next steps I recommend now:
- Hold on prefetch until we validate stability for 30 minutes.
- Stand up a canary to shift 10% traffic to rdw-instruct-v2-compact immediately (routing config). If p99 and QPS improve at canary, escalate to 50% over 20m.
- Prepare rollback plan if compact shows quality regressions; QA team on call for sampling.

Customer-facing draft (Alicia / Checkoutly ops) — feel free to edit: 
---
We observed an operational surge impacting Checkoutly’s generation latency and throughput. We’ve applied a temporary protection policy to stabilize traffic and increased internal caching to reduce recompute. We are also running a short canary that routes a small portion of traffic to a lower-compute model variant as a fallback. We expect reduced tail latency within ~30 minutes and will update you again at +60m.
---

I’ve attached the runbook Ben referenced and a short customer note draft.

Alicia — quick update and customer note for your channel.

Status (15:02 PT):
- Actions taken: soft token shed + KV TTL increase applied at 09:19 PT; 10% canary to rdw-instruct-v2-compact running from 09:35 PT.
- Impact: p99 improved from ~1.8s -> ~480–650ms. QPS trending back toward baseline.
- Next: we’ll hold the canary and, if no quality regressions in 20–30m, ramp to 50% to recover throughput faster. Rollback plan is ready if needed.

Customer-facing note (please copy/paste into your ops or status channel):
---
We experienced a transient performance regression that increased response times for generation. Redwood has applied temporary protective controls (rate shedding and increased caching) and is running a short canary to route a small portion of traffic to a lower-compute model to accelerate recovery. We expect tail latency to remain elevated for up to 30 minutes while we validate, with incremental improvements thereafter. Redwood will post a follow-up in 60 minutes with the final remediation steps and any further actions.

If you’d like additional wording (shorter or more technical) I can tailor it. Confirm you’re good to publish and I’ll also post the link to the runbook for your on-call if you want it.

—Monica
